title: Clearly I’m *so* excited about all of these! 😅 #broadway #musicalthea...
transcript: Ranking the five Grammy nominees for Best Musical Theater Album Except I'm ranking them by a very specific metric, so listen closely. How well does each album serve as an ambassador for the material? And that includes the quality of the score, but not exclusively. So in last place, I have Two Strangers Carry a Cake Across New York. And this is a case where I liked the show, but I don't think the score is its strongest asset. So if I listen to this, I probably would assume I wouldn't like the show. And for a completely different reason, I have Ragtime in 4th place, because this is obviously one of the greatest scores of the last several decades. The thing for me here is, even though this is a very good album, because we already have the original, and it's just so freaking good, I don't think I would ever be drawn to re-listen to this recording, specifically. even though I love Joshua Henry, I just think I would default to the original. just to prove my point that this is not about how much I like the music: Next I have Schmigadoon, which is a show that was very much not for me, but, you know, it's a solid album, it does convey what the musical is like, and it stands apart well enough from the TV soundtrack. Next I have chess. And, you know, I was deeply critical of this production, especially the performances from Aaron Tveit and Lea Michele. But, you know, the vocals were not my problem with the performances, and the score is certainly not my problem with the show. So having this fairly complete recording with modern production that isn't a live album, I think it's a totally worthwhile edition to the Chess recording canon. And in first place, surprising even myself, I have Lost Boys, another show that I was very critical of, and I was even critical of the score. But I have to admit that listening to the album, I liked the music more, and I liked more *of* the music than I did listening to it in the theatre. There are really fun parts of this score that the album does capture well. And I can skip past the boring stuff at my pleasure on the album, which I can't do in the theatre.
